newsitem.title: USA: IBM plans 50 bln yen dual-currency samurai.
newsitem.headline: IBM plans 50 bln yen dual-currency samurai.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp is expected to announce as early as Friday a 50 billion yen dual-currency samurai bond issue, a source close to the deal said.
The issue would be the third of its kind since IBM sold 50 billion yen worth of 5.3 percent yen/U.S. dollar dual currency samurais due 1999 in September via lead manager Daiwa Securities Co Ltd.
Another 50 billion yen worth of yen/U.S. dollar dual-currency samurais due in 2000 were issued by IBM through Daiwa in November.

An underwriting source on Thursday said the denominations of the planned issue had yet to be determined. In November, sources said the bonds could be launched in either yen/Australian dollar denominations or yen/U.S. dollars.
Under the previous structures, the coupon payments were to be paid in yen, while the redemptions will be in U.S. dollars.
Both prior issues were rated A1 by Moody's Investors Service and single-A by Standard & Poor's.
(( -- Al Yoon, U.S. Corporate Bonds Unit, 212-859-1672 ))
